checks: No eclipse at 1 of 5 covered epochs where the 4.43022 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 348791607 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.4302 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse that dims the light by 1.71 percent, with a strong detection signal-to-noise of 48.1 using the Box Least Squares method. Pixel-level image analysis provides additional support, revealing a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 16.0 and a centroid offset of 1.4 arcseconds from the target position. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. Notably, this candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be previously unknown. The automated pipeline assigned it a machine-learning screening score of 0.46, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
